data.rationale: When the savefile linktype is DLT_USB_LINUX_MMAPPED, fixup_pcap_pkthdr casts the packet data buffer to pcap_usb_header_mmapped* and dereferences usb_hdr->data_flag, usb_hdr->ndesc and usb_hdr->urb_len (lines 1853-1855) without any check that hdr->caplen is at least sizeof(pcap_usb_header_mmapped) (~64 bytes). Reachability from the fuzz target: fuzz_pcap -> pcap_open_offline with a pcap file whose header sets a small snaplen; sf-pcap.c:400-402 sizes p->bufsize as min(snapshot, 2048) and mallocs exactly that (e.g. 20 bytes). pcap_next_packet (sf-pcap.c:559-705) only grows the buffer to fit caplen, then calls fixup_pcap_pkthdr (sf-pcap.c:711) unconditionally. With caplen < 64 the reads at offsets ~56-63 fall outside the malloc'd region -> ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ. In contrast, the callee fix_linux_usb_mmapped_length (pcap-usb-linux-common.c:44-50) and every swap_*_header function in pcap-common.c properly bounds-check caplen before touching USB/pseudo-header fields; fixup_pcap_pkthdr is the only consumer of this data lacking that guard, so it is the root cause.
